title: P1-02 — Owner-controlled persistent parent VM and SSH
objective: Implement one owner-operated protected parent Dev VM that persists across SSH/OpenCode disconnects and has no default lifetime cap, with explicit stop and identity-bound recovery. Architecture skeleton (Claude review pending): stable parent identity owns persistent private guest data; per-boot run identity owns volatile QEMU/proxy/virtiofs/logger and transport artifacts; reuse v3 launch/identity/ordered-cleanup machinery with explicit ephemeral-smoke versus persistent-parent artifact policy. #55 supplies the protected pinned-2.2.5 OpenCode/session seam; #56 supplies a separate restricted per-run metrics-key and 500-ms push hook in the same boot lifecycle. No child orchestration.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run a single owner-controlled parent Dev VM through the protected project script with lifecycle start, status, SSH, and deliberate stop operations. No general multi-VM orchestration. The parent remains running when SSH disconnects or OpenCode exits and supports reconnect without restart.

No default parent-VM or OpenCode session wall-clock cap, idle shutdown, or forced session termination. An optional owner-configured maximum lifetime is disabled by default for the parent; policy can represent future mandatory child-VM limits without implementing child orchestration.

Owner host-to-guest SSH uses the existing protected per-VM identity, verified host key, private state, fixed trusted executable/configuration policy, interactive PTY, EscapeChar=none, and terminal restoration. Disable agent/X11 forwarding and arbitrary tunnels/forwarding changes. Disconnect/reconnect must not restart the parent. Remote owner access is documented via an approved authenticated host SSH/VPN hop, never public guest SSH or router forwarding.

Parent stop/up preserves the same protected private persistent guest disk, authorized workspace selection/data, OpenCode configuration, provider auth state, and session history. Auth remains available after reboot until provider expiry/revocation, explicit logout, or owner-authorized reset. A genuinely new parent gets fresh state. Ordinary stop/recovery never deletes parent disk or auth; destructive reset is separate and explicit. Credentials remain guest-private and are never exported to host workspace, logs, metrics or another VM; no unreviewed host escrow/backup system.

Explicit owner stop and ordinary SIGINT/SIGHUP/launcher failure produce bounded identity-bound teardown and independently verifiable stopped state. A minimal owner-only recovery/verification path handles SIGKILL or launcher loss using validated run identity, executable/start-time/argv, pidfd where available, listener and artifact checks; never trust PID-file contents, kill ambiguous/unrelated processes, or reuse smoke-report-bound --verify-cleanup for arbitrary sessions.

Preserve the explicitly selected private bounded workspace and current hard isolation. Investigate the minimum safe writable development workspace; do not silently expand the existing 64-MiB noexec smoke export or expose broader host filesystem. Any size/backing-store authority increase requires explicit owner approval.

Final owner tests prove script start/status/SSH/stop/reconnect, OpenCode exit/reconnect and session continuation, unlimited default lifetime, stop/up persistence of disk/workspace/config/auth/session history, auth expiry/logout/reset semantics, fresh new-parent state, explicit destructive-reset behavior, SIGINT/SIGHUP cleanup, controlled SIGKILL recovery, stale/mismatched identity refusal, no unrelated process termination, PTY restoration, no host Docker socket, and bounded workspace isolation. No VM action is run without owner authorization.

needed: Owner approval for foreground lifecycle/recovery trust boundary and finite deadline.
PTY and resize tests; SIGINT/SIGHUP cleanup; SIGKILL orphan recovery with exact-identity fixtures and host canary.
Full protected smoke on final SHA after any launcher/provisioning change.
Protected script lifecycle start/status/ssh/stop; PTY reconnect and OpenCode exit independence.
No default expiry/idle shutdown; optional max-lifetime policy disabled for parent.
Identity-bound SIGINT/SIGHUP/stop cleanup and owner-only SIGKILL recovery/verification; no PID-file authority.
Per-VM authenticated SSH from owner host and approved remote host-hop, no unapproved forwarding.
Workspace-size/backing review and explicit owner approval before any export expansion.
No runtime testing until owner authorizes the specific host action.

Owner-authorized real-process and owner-VM checks for stop/up preserving the same parent disk, workspace, OpenCode config, auth and session history; verify fresh state only for new parent or explicit owner reset.
